diff --git a/internal/store/sqlite.go b/internal/store/sqlite.go
index e55c600..d93ca59 100644
--- a/internal/store/sqlite.go
+++ b/internal/store/sqlite.go
@@ -20,20 +20,35 @@ import (
 // DBName is the file Open creates in the data directory.
 const DBName = "notes.db"
 
-// timeLayout is SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP text: UTC to the second, ordered
-// and compared as text, parsed back by parseTime.
+// timeLayout is how this store writes a note's times: UTC text, ordered and
+// compared as text, parsed back by parseTime. The seconds may carry a
+// fractional part, which layoutFor answers; users and sessions keep SQLite's
+// own second-precision CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.
 const timeLayout = "2006-01-02 15:04:05"
 
+// stampLayout is timeLayout with milliseconds, enough for two notes written
+// in the same second to hold a strict order of their own.
+const stampLayout = "2006-01-02 15:04:05.000"
+
+// layoutFor picks the layout that reads a stored time back: the plain second
+// when it carries no fraction, milliseconds when it does.
+func layoutFor(text string) string {
+	if len(text) > len(timeLayout) && text[len(timeLayout)] == '.' {
+		return stampLayout
+	}
+	return timeLayout
+}
+
 var migrationName = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9]{14}_[a-z0-9_]+\.sql$`)
 
 type sqliteStore struct {
 	db *sql.DB
 
 	// stampMu guards lastStamp: the newest note timestamp this store wrote.
-	// SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP only turns with the second, so notes written
-	// inside one second would share it and a listing ordered by updated_at
-	// could not tell an edit from the rows it has to come before. Each write
-	// therefore takes at least the second after the previous stamp.
+	// A listing orders notes by updated_at, so a write must never share or
+	// fall behind the stamp of the row it has to come after. Stamps carry
+	// milliseconds and move on by one when the clock has not caught up, which
+	// keeps the order strict without ever pushing a note into the future.
 	stampMu   sync.Mutex
 	lastStamp time.Time
 }

detail.text:
`bash check` passes (web lint/tests/build, vet, gofmt, gosec, `go test -race`).

The card's listing/search/pin API and `Notes.tsx` were already in place from the earlier attempt; I addressed its findings: note timestamps are now millisecond stamps that only ever lag or match the wall clock (the old per-write +1s bump inflated `updated_at` system-wide), parsing/formatting handles both forms, and the API emits fixed-width RFC 3339 times so a client comparing them as text can't misorder `.835Z` vs `.83Z`. The pin-ordering tests and store build are verified green with `-count=2`. Recommend merging.
